## Context / Problem
The outbound Jira comment dedup key is one composition of functions in the differ; the send is a different composition in the adapter. Every convergence bug has been a point where the two drifted:
- `fit_comment_as_sent` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_comments.py:283`) re-runs the send's fit to stay equal to `add_comment` (`adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py:531`).
- The truncation suffix literal lives in three places (`adapters/jira/comment_limits.py:46`, `adapters/jira/adf.py:333`, `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py:69`); the limit in four (32767 x3 vs 32000 at `adf.py:332`).
- Decoration happens in the differ and fitting in the adapter, shearing the marker (`unreal-empathetic-illadopsis`).

Landed fixes `8209097fa9` (one decoder) and `46575522d6` (DC fit on the send path) corrected two drifts, but the structure that produced five tickets (`irongrey-chubby-oxpecker`, `abusive-pebbly-sakimonkey`, `aragonite-bleached-vipersquid`, `unreal-empathetic-illadopsis`, `community-sediment-snipe`) remains. This story is the structural remedy.

The remaining gap is narrow and real: **the key PREDICTS the wire the send path will produce, rather than being taken from the bytes actually sent.** (The normalisation asymmetry at `outbound_comments.py:565-578` is already closed by bug `17c3-2f6e-a5e0-438c`, which made BOTH keys derive through `_normalize_comment_body`; it is not what this leaf targets.)

## Approach
Add `fit_for_send(body, codec, fit) -> FittedComment(landed_text, wire_body)` in `outbound_comments.py` (core names no vendor; `fit` is injected):
- `wire_body = fit_preserving_marker(decorate(body), fit)`, computed once.
- `landed_text = strip_marker(codec.decode_inbound(codec.to_wire(wire_body)))`.

The differ keys on `landed_text`; the mutation entry carries `wire_body`; Cloud and DC `add_comment` only encode and send. One suffix literal in `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`; the copies are deleted.

## Guard construction
Follow the guard-test construction rule in the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: owner module exempt, match the constituent conjunction or AST shape named in Approach (or the definition count where no distinctive atom exists), `# <construct>-ok: <reason>` escape marker, and behaviour pinned only by the named existing tests.

## Constraint: the sourced `32767` occurrences must SURVIVE
`32767` occurs in FOUR files under `src/rebar/_engine`, and most occurrences are legitimate:
- `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py:41` `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` — Cloud's limit (in scope);
- `rebar_reconciler/runtime.py:46` `_DEFAULT_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` — the runtime default;
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py:60,64` — the DC `jira.text.field.character.limit` `default-value`, quoted from Atlassian docs;
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:244-257` — PROSE citing JRASERVER-28519 for why 32767 is the DC default and why it is only a default.

Deleting those would delete sourced product knowledge. The construct being consolidated is the **fit-for-send composition**, not the number, so the acceptance oracle is behavioural (the key comes from the bytes sent), NOT a count of a magic number.

## Constraint: BOTH mutation-enactment consumers are in Scope
Two structurally identical consumers, not one. Scoping only the first would leave the update path sending the un-fitted `body` while the key came from `wire_body` — the exact drift this leaf closes, on half the traffic:
- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py:368-379` (create path);
- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py:375-384` (update path) — same `entry.get("body", "")` read, same single-attempt `client.add_comment(issue_key, body)`, same `_record_comment_id` follow-up.

Both pass `entry["wire_body"]`, falling back to `body` only for entries written before the cutover, so an in-flight queue does not break.

## Constraint: the `fit_comment` port keeps its contract
`_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py:481` declares the `fit_comment(self, body: str) -> str` Protocol, contract "return exactly the marker-free body the backend's SEND path lands". Implementers: `adapters/jira/backend.py:154` (Cloud) and `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:303` (DC), both delegating to `outbound_comments.fit_comment_as_sent` (`outbound_comments.py:290`).

**Decision: `fit_comment_as_sent` is RETAINED as a thin wrapper** — `fit_for_send(...).landed_text` — so the Protocol's `-> str` signature and both implementers keep working unchanged. Only callers needing the wire bytes move to `fit_for_send`, confining the change to the dedup-key path.

## Constraint: one codec, one set of bytes
- `acli_cli_ops.add_comment:531`, `adapters/jira/backend.add_comment` and DC's `sanitize_comment` **stop fitting/encoding independently** — each re-derives the body today, which is how key and sent bytes drift apart.
- `wire_body` is carried on the mutation entry, so the bytes are computed once.
- The send path MUST NOT re-encode: it writes `wire_body` verbatim. Where an adapter genuinely must encode at send time, it receives **the same codec instance** `fit_for_send` was given, asserted by an identity test — a second codec instance, or a second read of the cutover flag, re-opens the drift.

## Scope
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_comments.py`, `_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py`, `_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py`, `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py`, `adapters/jira/backend.py`, `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`, `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`, `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py`, `adapters/jira/adf.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fit_for_send.py` (new).

## Testing
Happy path over the captured corpus `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/bodies_*.json`: for every body, `landed_text` equals the decoded readback of `wire_body`. Edge: an over-limit body keeps the marker and the key still matches; DC bodies fit at `comment_max_chars()`. Pinning: `tests/unit/test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py`, `test_dc_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py`, `test_outbound_comment_marker_survives_truncation.py`, `test_acli_comment_adf_encode.py`, `test_rich_text_codec.py`, `test_backend_neutrality.py` pass unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The dedup key is derived from the bytes actually handed to the transport; checked by a test that fits an over-long comment and asserts key == hash(wire_body) == hash(what the fake transport received).
- [ ] For every corpus body, `landed_text` equals the decoded readback of `wire_body`; checked by the new corpus test.
- [ ] BOTH enactment consumers (`dispatch_one.py` create, `dispatch_apply_phases.py` update) send `wire_body`; checked by a test driving each path through a fake transport.
- [ ] `add_comment` performs no independent fit/encode; checked by a test asserting a fake codec is invoked exactly once per outbound comment.
- [ ] The send path uses the SAME codec instance (or the precomputed `wire_body`) that `fit_for_send` used; checked by an identity assertion in that test.
- [ ] `fit_comment_as_sent` and the `_backend.fit_comment` Protocol keep their `-> str` contract; checked by both backend implementers (`adapters/jira/backend.py:154`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:303`) passing unchanged.
- [ ] A mutation entry written before the cutover (no `wire_body`) still sends, on BOTH paths; checked by a back-compat test.
- [ ] The sourced `32767` occurrences in `runtime.py`, DC `settings.py` and DC `backend.py` prose are unchanged; checked by `git diff --stat`.
- [ ] The truncation suffix literal exists once under `src/rebar` (owner `jira_family/rich_text.py` exempt), and the pinning suites pass unchanged; checked by the guard test and `pytest`.
